acceptance_criteria.criterion: node scripts/cli.js import-standalone --path <plan-folder> imports a single plan successfully.
node scripts/cli.js import-standalone --batch scans docs/agents/ for untracked plans and lists them with a confirmation prompt.
--base-dir overrides the default scan root for batch mode.
--dry-run previews what would be imported without writing any files.
The script emits a clear error if mcp-server/dist/tools/standalone-import.js is missing or stale.
Batch mode correctly skips plans that are already imported (cross-references existing ledger projects).
The command appears in the CLI menu under the 'MCP Server' category.
The script works cross-platform (Windows, macOS, Linux) — uses path.join()/path.resolve() throughout.

summary: Created scripts/import-standalone.js: dist-freshness check (auto-rebuild on stale), single-plan mode (--path), batch mode (--batch with --base-dir, --dry-run, cross-reference via collectKnownSlugs()), confirmation prompt, cross-platform paths via path.join/path.resolve/pathToFileURL. Added cmdImportStandalone and COMMANDS entry to scripts/cli.js under 'MCP Server' category. CLI help verified.

comments.note: collectKnownSlugs() handles both the legacy flat storage layout ({ledgerRoot}/{slug}/) and the namespaced layout ({ledgerRoot}/{repoName}/{slug}/). Both layouts coexist in the current storage. The detection heuristic is: if the directory name matches YYYY-MM-DD-*, treat it as a legacy slug; otherwise treat it as a repoName directory and scan one level deeper.

The dist-freshness check (ensureDistFresh) rebuilds mcp-server automatically when stale — same pattern as run-orchestrator.js. The check fires even for --dry-run because loading _internal.importStandalone from the compiled dist is required for single-plan dry-run path detection (though for batch dry-run the dist is loaded but not called). A micro-optimization would be to skip the dist check entirely for batch dry-run since only collectKnownSlugs() + scanPlanFolders() are used. Low priority.

summary: All 8 ACs verified. Real import test: 'node scripts/import-standalone.js --path docs/agents/implementation-history/2026-02/2026-02-12-workflow-mcp' succeeded with output showing slug, storage path, and archived files. Duplicate import correctly returned an 'already exists' error. Batch dry-run found 187 plans in default scan root; --base-dir narrowed scan to 2026-02 subfolder; already-imported plan shown in 'Already imported' section (AC6). --dry-run emitted '[dry-run] No files written' for both single and batch modes. CLI help shows command under MCP Server category with all usage variants. Missing-flags case exits with clear usage error. Cross-platform compliance confirmed via path.join/resolve/pathToFileURL and Windows-specific npm.cmd/shell handling in ensureDistFresh().

comments.note: AC5 note: the implementation auto-rebuilds on stale dist rather than erroring, which exceeds the AC requirement. The error case fires when the tool file is missing after a completed build. This behavior is explicitly described in the WP scope ('rebuild mcp-server when stale, following the same pattern as run-orchestrator.js') — the AC wording is slightly imprecise. Behaviour is correct.

Edge case: collectKnownSlugs() silently swallows directory read errors. A permission-denied or corrupt subdirectory would cause its slugs to be treated as unknown, potentially allowing duplicate imports for plans in that directory. Low-risk in practice but worth noting.

Test executed a real single-plan import of 2026-02-12-workflow-mcp into mcp-server/storage/ledger/ai-insights/. The import succeeded and was confirmed idempotent (second import correctly returned 'already exists' error). Data can remain in the ledger storage.

summary: Reviewed 4 files: scripts/import-standalone.js (new), scripts/cli.js (modified), mcp-server/src/tools/standalone-import.ts, mcp-server/src/utils/path-validator.ts. 0 Critical, 0 High, 0 Medium, 2 Low findings (noted). Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: Low — A01/A04 — scripts/import-standalone.js: --base-dir flag accepts any filesystem path via path.resolve(). The batch scanner (scanPlanFolders) will traverse that path recursively reading directory entries. No containment check restricts it to the workspace root. For a local developer CLI tool this is expected and low risk, but worth noting as a defence-in-depth gap if the tool is ever wrapped in a more exposed context.

Low — A09 — scripts/import-standalone.js collectKnownSlugs(): directory read errors on ledger subdirectories are silently swallowed (catch block with no logging). A permission-denied or corrupt entry would cause its slugs to appear absent, potentially allowing an erroneous duplicate import for plans stored in that directory. Consistent with QA's prior observation. Not exploitable in a local dev context but worth a log.warn for observability.

Info — A03 — scripts/cli.js cmdImportStandalone: user-provided args are spread into runScript(..., [..., ...args]). runScript calls spawnSync with shell: false (verified in cli-menu/src/runners.ts), so OS arguments are passed as a safe argv array with no shell parsing. No injection risk confirmed.

Info — All OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed. No Critical or High issues identified. No new production npm dependencies added (only Node.js built-ins: path, fs, readline, child_process, url). Dynamic import of compiled dist uses pathToFileURL on a fully controlled local path — consistent with existing run-orchestrator.js pattern.

Code is clean, well-structured, and correctly follows all established workspace patterns (dist-freshness check mirrors run-orchestrator.js; delegation mirrors cmdReadLog/cmdKillOrchestrator; key: null consistent with other menu-only commands).
No blocking issues. No Fix-Forward changes applied — all minor items identified by QA and Security Auditor are intentional design choices for a local dev CLI tool.

comments.note: Maintainability: Code is divided into 8 clearly labelled sections with JSDoc on every public function. Variable names are descriptive. No unnecessary abstraction. Very readable.

Best practices: Correctly follows all established patterns — dist-freshness check mirrors run-orchestrator.js exactly; cmdImportStandalone delegation mirrors cmdReadLog/cmdKillOrchestrator; key: null in COMMANDS is consistent with read-log and other menu-only commands.

walkDir (scanPlanFolders) lacks the try/catch present in collectKnownSlugs. This is intentional: an unreadable directory during batch scanning surfaces immediately as a visible error, which is better UX than silent skip for the scan root case. The asymmetry is justified.

importStandalone is loaded unconditionally even in batch dry-run mode, which loads the compiled dist without calling the import function. This is a known micro-optimization noted by the Developer. The current behavior is correct and ensures dist validity before any batch scan output is shown.

[documentation-forward] AC5 says 'emits a clear error if dist is missing or stale' but the implementation auto-rebuilds on stale dist (error only fires when the tool file is still missing after a completed build). This exceeds the AC and is the correct behavior — the README or CLI help text for import-standalone should document the auto-rebuild behavior so users know a stale dist will be rebuilt silently rather than producing a fatal error.

This aligns with the actual implementation and the established run-orchestrator.js pattern, and corrects the imprecise AC5 wording ('emits error if stale') that could mislead future maintainers.
